exact_statement: For a normalized finite reference S, vacuum calibration C_p(S), and any positive mass-preserving frequency map M fixing the empty point mass, C_r(M C_p(S))=C_r(M S) whenever p<1 and the final calibration is admissible; the constant-parent case p=1 also holds for physical Boolean descendants, which necessarily have r=1. Consequently every finite adaptive physical-query policy returning repeatedly to the direct marginal of ONE fixed original source followed by vacuum calibration is pathwise identical to calibrating the CURRENT inherited reference after its first reset, provided intervening operations are only physical frequency deletions and vacuum calibrations. Under the explicitly supplied A096 likelihood hypotheses, all erasures and full terminal cross entropies therefore remain bounded by c+(1-m^2)log2(1/gamma), with zero surcharge for the number of returns. This supplies neither a universally influence-priced reference nor a likelihood floor for arbitrary Boolean functions.

M is positive and mass preserving and sends delta_empty to delta_empty; physical maps delete queried frequency coordinates.
ONE fixed original source throughout each exit; no new edit floor, nonempty-shape change or source replacement between calibrations.
